clue.text: Marvellous Scot'S left political group

parts.note: fab is informal for marvellous
Ian is a typical Scottish first name, so a Scot's is IAN'S

explanation.surface: A wonderful Scotsman has quit some political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fabian Society is a long-standing British socialist group, the 'left political group' here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fabians are members of a British socialist society, hence a group on the political left.

clue.text: Peasant died — what a shame!

parts.note: fell means died, as of soldiers in battle
ah is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over news of a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellah is a farm worker in Arab countries, especially Egypt.

clue.text: Plant showing insect damage

parts.note: a bug is an insect
loss means damage or harm

explanation.surface: A garden shrub shows signs of pest attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly flowering herb of the borage family.

clue.text: Mechanic and I refit car that's been damaged

indicators.note: damage puts things out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A garage worker and I repair a damaged vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or military mechanic.

clue.text: Forcibly crush bread in vessel

indicators.note: the bread word is placed inside the vessel word

parts.note: a steamer is a ship
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Someone squashes a loaf on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To steamroller opposition is to overwhelm it by brute force.

clue.text: Girl put on coat for play

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece put on another is added after it

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat (short for mackintosh)
Beth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl puts on her coat before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Scottish king is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Forcefully beat up and disfigure

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ram is to strike forcefully

explanation.surface: A thug beats someone up and leaves scars.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or damage the appearance of something.

clue.text: French chemist said nothing, a strange person

indicators.note: the name is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: Marie Curie, the Paris-based Nobel chemist
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A French scientist said nothing and seemed an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is an oddity; applied to people it means a peculiar character.

clue.text: I've no problem — useless being discontented

indicators.note: the words are a problem to be worked out, so their letters are mixed

parts.note: US, short for unserviceable, means useless

explanation.surface: Someone claims no trouble, though feeling futile and dissatisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Envious people resent what others have, so they are dissatisfied.

clue.text: Level of standards dropped in some respect

definitions.text: Level of standards dropped in some respect

parts.words: Level of standards dropped in some respect
parts.note: standards are flags, lowered partway as a mark of respect or mourning

explanation.surface: Values have slipped somewhat in certain ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags flown partway down a pole show mourning, a lowered position.

clue.text: A girl they maltreated for so very long

indicators.note: treated badly, so the letters of the words before it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl was mistreated for an extremely long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so very long' is a playful definition: the distance light travels in a year is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: A light year is a vast astronomical distance, figuratively an immense span.

clue.text: Discover there isn't a feast

indicators.note: says the following letter is absent from the word before

parts.note: to discover a secret is to reveal it

explanation.surface: Someone finds out there will be no banquet after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively celebration, much like a festive party.

clue.text: Uninvolved in a hoax that backfires

indicators.note: something that backfires goes the wrong way, so the word for hoax is read backwards

parts.note: to hoax someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: Someone stays detached from a practical joke that goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof keeps distant and detached, taking no part.

clue.text: It's a small world!

parts.note: the familiar remark about coincidences read literally: something that is a world in miniature

explanation.surface: The stock exclamation on meeting an acquaintance unexpectedly far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature representation of a larger system is literally a little world.

clue.text: Prison and hard labour, possibly?

definitions.meaning: the old word for childbirth, which may be a hard labour

explanation.surface: A convict faces jail with hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being locked up and the period of giving birth.

clue.text: Horror film review is a study in the mind's depths

definitions.text: a study in the mind's depths

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 horror film
a review is an analysis or examination

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a scary movie delves into the unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's method explores the unconscious, the deep levels of a patient's thought.

clue.text: Eventually team-mate gets on side

parts.note: later means eventually
an ally is a partner on the same side

explanation.surface: In time, a fellow player joins the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, toward or from the flank.

clue.text: Unlike Blakeney, you heard shotgun going off

parts.note: the word you pronounced gives the letter U

indicators.note: a gun going off is fired; the letters of shotgun explode into a new order

explanation.surface: A gun fires, contrasting someone with a famous hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Percy Blakeney is the Scarlet Pimpernel: 'They seek him here, they seek him there', so he was much sought.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional hero was hunted everywhere; the opposite is not looked for.

clue.text: A look at life unaffected by past record

parts.note: unaffected behaviour is natural
a history is a record of the past

explanation.surface: An honest documentary about life free of any old baggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of plants and animals examines living things, a survey of biology.

clue.text: Material for over-rich cheese

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: fat means rich, as of food
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Fabric that is too fatty, like cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp shiny silk or synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Crowd's murmuring for food

definitions.meaning: actors in a crowd scene repeat a nonsense word to sound like background chatter
the pink stalks are cooked as a fruit

explanation.surface: Diners grumble over the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a stage crowd's background noise and an edible plant stalk.

clue.text: Hell, the French do interrupt rudely

parts.note: heck is a mild substitute for hell
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone curses, the French barracking loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to shout taunts at a speaker.

clue.text: Naturally receiving fine for going in wrong direction

indicators.note: the phrase takes the letter in, so it goes inside

parts.note: 'of course' means naturally
F is the abbreviation for fine (on pencils)

explanation.surface: Unsurprisingly, a driver heading the wrong way gets a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or plane straying from its route travels the wrong way.

clue.text: You'll find her in high spirits

definitions.text: You'll find her in high spirits

parts.words: You'll find her in high spirits
parts.note: high spirits read as spirits of high places: a nymph of the mountains, not a cheerful mood

explanation.surface: A woman is always cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this kind of nymph lives on mountains.

clue.text: Ruddy cheeky stuff as girl's first grabbed by lecher

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the word for lecher

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word girl's

explanation.surface: A bloody impudent lecher grabs a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' reads as a mild curse but is the colour, and 'cheeky' means for the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cosmetic powder is applied to give the cheeks a reddish glow.

clue.text: In delight, bishop gives land to clergy

indicators.note: the letter for bishop goes inside the word for delight

parts.note: glee is delight
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A happy bishop donates property to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a parish priest's benefice included farmland to support him.

clue.text: Woman will support old sailor

parts.note: she'll is short for 'she will'
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A woman promises to stand by an elderly seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellback is slang for a veteran seaman, especially one who has crossed the equator.

clue.text: Woman is separated from children

indicators.note: the word is is taken away from the children word

parts.note: issue means offspring

explanation.surface: A mother is parted from her kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a female first name.

clue.text: Toddler's beginning to walk on short legs? Nonsense!

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Toddler's is used

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with short rocking steps

explanation.surface: A toddler starts to walk on stubby legs, though someone scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly talk, rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Historian has been upset by a trifle

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of 'been' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar is disturbed by something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' may suggest the pudding; here it is a trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Toynbee was a British scholar who wrote A Study of History.
